outline.heading: His courage and selflessness
outline.gist: Leaving dependent daughters behind for Allah's sake required near-impossible courage and selflessness.

outline.heading: 'Send me back': the verse is revealed
outline.gist: He asked to return and fight again; refused, he asked that those behind be told of his bliss, and the verses came down.

outline.heading: Interlude
Those who love praise for what they did not do
outline.gist: A frightening verse about people made vain by wealth, fame, status or accomplishments who want credit that is not theirs.

outline.heading: What can you truly claim credit for?
outline.gist: You may have participated, but claiming the whole credit and wanting praise for it is another matter.

outline.heading: Vanity is punishable
outline.gist: They will not escape punishment.

outline.heading: Success can go to your head over time
outline.gist: Young people can keep the balance, but repeated success can turn into lecturing others on why you succeeded and they failed.

outline.heading: Turn your hands up in gratitude
outline.gist: When Allah grants you something great, answer with humble gratitude for a gift you do not deserve and use it to please Him.

outline.heading: Allah rarely states what He wants; here He does
outline.gist: In the part of the surah on values, He spells out His will because values cannot be accepted without understanding what He intends.

outline.heading: He wants to make things clear to you
outline.gist: The mind is an unmatched tool; once you understand you submit, and once you submit you find fulfilment.

outline.heading: No one commits to what he does not understand
outline.gist: The ummah struggles because we expect commitment without investing in clarity about who Allah is and why He is worth living for.

outline.heading: To guide you in the ways of the prophets before you
outline.gist: You hold a treasure carrying the guidance of Adam, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and the rest, yet spend time on other things.

outline.heading: He wants to turn to you in mercy
outline.gist: When people are wronged they want justice or to see the wrongdoer fall; when you wrong Allah's rights, He wants you to repent and improve.

outline.heading: Even parents want a little punishment
outline.gist: Most parents want their children to reform but with some punishment to feel better; Allah wants no punishment for you.

outline.heading: Those who follow desires want you to deviate entirely
outline.gist: They want you to lose every attachment to this way of life.

outline.heading: He wants to lighten your burden
outline.gist: The fourth wish: a light load so you can carry it, excel and reach your true potential.

outline.heading: 'Where is the ease in fasting and no bars?'
outline.gist: Young people ask where the ease is when they cannot drink, take drugs or have girlfriends; that is exactly where it is.

outline.heading: Ramadan shows how easy you had it
outline.gist: Working without food or sleep reveals how much you had all year and how self-centred you were not to see it.

outline.heading: Following desires is a black hole
outline.gist: It sucks the life out of you until you lose your spirit and identity, anxious about what comes when the lights go out.

outline.heading: The happiest person is the one connected to Allah
outline.gist: Standing in prayer with only Allah in your heart brings a fulfilment so deep that losing a little sends you running back to it.

themes.label: Values, principles and ethics as a system
themes.note: An-Nisa' teaches the values behind its laws, and a value is only real when applied to the weak as much as the strong.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: Knowing each surah's theme gives direction when reciting and reflecting.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Paradise requires proving yourself: strive in ease and persevere in hardship.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: His smile, handshake, full attention and readiness to solve people's problems show the gentleness Allah gave him.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: Despite the archers' costly mistake he was told to pardon them and seek forgiveness for them.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions
themes.note: Consultation is binding on leaders even after a consultation went wrong; then decide and trust Allah.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Repentance does not entitle you to an easy road; expect repeated falls and remember Allah owes you nothing.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: Those killed in Gaza while staying on their land are martyrs, though Muslims mourn rather than celebrate death.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: Jabir's father went out at Uhud with rare courage and selflessness and was honoured by his Lord.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Vanity and claiming credit for what Allah gave you are punishable; answer success with humble gratitude.

themes.label: The purposes behind Allah's commands (maqasid)
themes.note: Allah states His will: to clarify, to guide in the prophets' ways, to accept repentance and to lighten the burden.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: Fasting shows how easy life was all along and where real ease lies.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: Desires drain the soul, while connection with Allah gives unmatched happiness.

quran.point: A parallel verse rebuking the assumption of entering Paradise without being tested.
The surah opens with the same idea: people will not be left to say they believe without being tested.

hadith.gist: Recite Al-Baqarah and Al 'Imran, for they will come on the Day of Resurrection shielding and pleading for their companions.
The Prophet would offer his hand first and not withdraw it until the other person did, and he turned his whole body toward whoever he spoke to.
At Uhud the Prophet told the archers not to leave their position even if they saw birds snatching the Muslims' bodies, until he sent for them.
The companions never saw the Prophet weep as he did on the day Hamza was killed.
When Jabir wept over his father, the Prophet said the angels kept shading him with their wings until he was raised.

Allah spoke to Jabir's father without a veil and invited him to wish; he asked to be sent back to be killed again, and when told none return he asked that those behind be informed, so 3:169 was revealed.

maxims: A value used selectively isn't a value
In ease strive, in hardship persevere
Consultation is not optional
Allah owes you nothing
We don't celebrate death; we are comforted
No one commits to what he doesn't understand

7eqRXRt2MuY.title: Ramadan: Our Turning Point
7eqRXRt2MuY.one_line: On the eve of Ramadan he blames Gaza's prolonged bloodshed partly on Muslim disorganization, urges a personal turning point, and gives a ten-point Ramadan plan.
7eqRXRt2MuY.summary: Speaking on the last Friday before Ramadan, he asks everyone to enter the month intending to make it a turning point, however many times they have tried before. He grounds that intention in his reading of Gaza: the regime kills freely because it has unconditional Western support, Western leaders give it because they answer only to money and votes, and they feel no pressure because Muslims in the West are disorganized. Muslims lack neither numbers, expertise nor wealth, only organization, having settled into comfortable self-centred lives and petty disputes such as moon sighting. He rejects an end-times passivity that waits for a hero; nobody is coming, and Allah placed each person here with a role. Any explanation of a disaster that leaves out our own shortcomings is not Islamic. He asks listeners to recover the idealistic younger self they once were, as the Prophet revived that spark in his companions, and to bring their regrets to Allah. In the second khutbah he lists ten points: intention, fasting from sin as well as food, congregational prayer and full taraweeh, daily Quran, dhikr, Islamic learning, repairing relationships, service to others, sincere dua, and half an hour of daily life planning.

outline.heading: Opening
One verse, one season, one ummah
outline.gist: The Ramadan verse is being recited on minbars across the Muslim world this week and the next; he finds beauty in Muslims recognising and embracing the same seasons together. On the last Friday before Ramadan he offers thoughts on making the most of it.

outline.heading: Make Ramadan a turning point
outline.gist: His motto: make this Ramadan a turning point, even if you have resolved to change before; there is no limit to how many times. Change on an inner level others cannot see, which will show over time in your decisions and choices. The intention needs a reason, which he grounds in the events of the last 150 days.

outline.heading: 150 days of bloodshed
outline.gist: Some 30,000 civilians killed in 150 days, most of them women and children, in the 21st century while the world watches, and people now being starved: how is this still going on?

outline.heading: Why it continues: unconditional support
outline.gist: The regime would not dare spill so much blood without unconditional support from the world's powers, Canada among them. Had it felt pressure from Western countries it would have held back, sought a deal for its hostages and looked for a ceasefire.

outline.heading: Leaders who worship money and votes
outline.gist: Western governments did not apply pressure because their leaders have no moral compass and worship money, votes and a skewed apocalyptic belief. They felt no pressure at home on re-election or finances, because we are disorganised.

outline.heading: We lack organisation, not numbers or wealth
outline.gist: Muslims in the West lack the financial and political ability to apply pressure, not numbers, expertise or wealth. Decades of colonialism and tyranny left many content with a self-centred life of family, savings, barbecues, cars and vacations.

outline.heading: Muslims were never self-centred
outline.gist: Accepting Islam once made a person alert to the world and outspoken for justice; becoming self-centred cost us the bigger picture. Organisation that changes policy does not happen overnight, since politicians believe only in what keeps them in office.

outline.heading: Too busy arguing about moon sighting
outline.gist: We did not do our job: we argued over moon sighting versus calculation and other petty matters as if we had the luxury, instead of working together and pooling wealth and time even with people we disagree with or dislike, since our interests are one. Part of the ummah paid for it in blood.

outline.heading: So now what?
outline.gist: Will Muslims in the West strengthen their community, give their youth identity, education and confidence, and fund groups that advocate so their voice is heard in policy, or go back to normal once a ceasefire comes? Most of us hold up four or five hands to block out what demands our effort.

outline.heading: The Armageddon mindset: nobody is coming
outline.gist: In Syria he worked against an end-times worldview that waits for prophesied events or for Muslims to become strong again. Nothing is coming, there is no hero on a bus: the people around you are all there is. The Prophet left a generation that dealt with problems personally.

outline.heading: You have a role
outline.gist: We have become a passive ummah asking why someone else does not speak; the only person who should speak is you. Allah put you here with a role; He would not have created you if He did not see something in you.

outline.heading: This will be our turning point
outline.gist: On the eve of Ramadan, intend: I will not go back to the same lifestyle; I will revise my choices, decisions and priorities. When you do, you will find others doing the same.

outline.heading: Fewer people with lesser reasons
outline.gist: You will have companionship; the community still cares, just not yet past the threshold needed to organise and make an impact. The world has been changed by fewer people with lesser reasons, while children die of preventable causes a few miles from help.

outline.heading: Your shortcoming is part of every explanation
outline.gist: Any theory of a disaster that leaves out your own shortcoming is not Islamic; the Quran never lets you look at a bad situation without seeing your share in it. If the mirror shows you a flawless person, you have bigger problems.

outline.heading: Bring back your younger self
outline.gist: Remember the idealistic, hopeful person you were at fifteen or twenty. Life's storms throw you around until you lose your bearings, but that person with the compass still lives inside you; find them and listen to them again.

outline.heading: The Prophet re-ignited his companions
outline.gist: He made people in their forties, fifties and sixties feel young again, kindling what they always knew was inside them under years of clutter, because he lived as that person himself.

outline.heading: Bring your regrets to the One who heals
outline.gist: That version of you is more committed, has more grit, is less selfish and above petty things. Enter Ramadan with it and you will weep over wasted time and mistakes, which is healthy, because you are crying to the One who listens, forgives and heals.

outline.heading: Interlude
Point one: intention
outline.gist: Of ten things to think about in Ramadan, intention comes first; nothing comes close to it in importance. With the right intention things change during the month and after.

outline.heading: Point two: fast from haram, a wider buffer
outline.gist: Fast with excellence: from haram, gossip, and what you should not see, hear or say, not only food and drink. Ramadan pushes the line so even halal food becomes forbidden by day, widening your buffer from haram and bringing your heart closer to Allah.

outline.heading: Point three: congregation and taraweeh to the end
outline.gist: Pray in congregation as a bare minimum and stand with the imam until he finishes taraweeh: we stand an hour and a half in line for food or a driver's licence. Open the Quran and follow along; if tired, sit or take a break and come back. Prayer improves with practice; choose the masjid closest to you and stay for witr and the dua.

outline.heading: Point four: the Quran without a middleman
outline.gist: Revive your relationship with the Quran: recite, memorise, understand. You need no interpreter between you and Allah; read a little every day. This book saved us and will save us again; until we return to it we stay lost.

outline.heading: Point five: dhikr in the hungry hours
outline.gist: When you are starving with a headache, instead of scrolling, say words that connect you to Allah and learn to find joy in His names.

outline.heading: Point six: Islamic knowledge
outline.gist: Invest in your Islamic understanding, not only academic education: attend a daily or weekly dars and keep it after Ramadan. He admits he now feels ashamed eating while people in Gaza fight over wheat; change starts with the spark Ramadan lights inside you, which later becomes advocacy, outreach and giving.

outline.heading: Point seven: repair relationships
outline.gist: Invest in your spouse and parents, call people you have not spoken to in years and mend broken relationships; the ummah cannot survive divided.

outline.heading: Point eight: service, rewarded twice
outline.gist: Serve others whether or not they appreciate it: sadaqah, helping the masjid run, minding children so others can pray. If you would otherwise be praying or reciting, you earn the reward of both, the best deal in Ramadan.

outline.heading: Point nine: the art of dua
outline.gist: Allah speaks to you through a book, so learn to converse with Him. Drop the formal job-interview dua with titles and signatures; speak to Him as you are, as creation to Creator.

outline.heading: Point ten: half an hour of planning a day
outline.gist: Put the phone away for thirty minutes a day and write who you hope to be, what you stand for and what legacy you will leave. The plan will almost always fail, but its skeleton keeps you yourself when life throws curveballs: fifteen years ago he had not even heard of London, Ontario. Especially for high school and university students.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.note: Enter every Ramadan intending it to be a turning point; there is no limit to how many times one can resolve to change.

themes.note: Western Muslims cannot pressure politicians because they are disorganized; they must fund and build advocacy groups so their voice is heard and respected in policy.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it

14:32.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ رِزۡقࣰ ا لَّكُمۡۖ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ لِتَجۡرِيَ فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِأَمۡرِهِۦۖ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرَ
14:32.en: It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth and sent down rain from the sky and produced thereby some fruits as provision for you and subjected for you the ships to sail through the sea by His command and subjected for you the rivers

14:33.en: And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, continuous [in orbit], and subjected for you the night and the day

29:17.ar: إِنَّمَا تَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوۡثَٰنࣰ ا وَتَخۡلُقُونَ إِفۡكًاۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَا يَمۡلِكُونَ لَكُمۡ رِزۡقࣰ ا فَٱبۡتَغُواْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرِّزۡقَ وَٱعۡبُدُوهُ وَٱشۡكُرُواْ لَهُۥٓۖ إِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ

2:172.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُلُواْ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡ وَٱشۡكُرُواْ لِلَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ إِيَّاهُ تَعۡبُدُونَ
2:172.en: O you who have believed, eat from the good things which We have provided for you and be grateful to Allah if it is [indeed] Him that you worship

51:22.en: And in the heaven is your provision and whatever you are promised

51:23.ar: فَوَرَبِّ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِنَّهُۥ لَحَقࣱّ مِّثۡلَ مَآ أَنَّكُمۡ تَنطِقُونَ

63:10.ar: وَأَنفِقُواْ مِن مَّا رَزَقۡنَٰكُم مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ فَيَقُولَ رَبِّ لَوۡلَآ أَخَّرۡتَنِيٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ قَرِيبࣲ فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
63:10.en: And spend [in the way of Allah] from what We have provided you before death approaches one of you and he says, "My Lord, if only You would delay me for a brief term so I would give charity and be among the righteous

15:20.ar: وَجَعَلۡنَا لَكُمۡ فِيهَا مَعَٰيِشَ وَمَن لَّسۡتُمۡ لَهُۥ بِرَٰزِقِينَ
15:20.en: And We have made for you therein means of living and [for] those for whom you are not providers

67:21.ar: أَمَّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي يَرۡزُقُكُمۡ إِنۡ أَمۡسَكَ رِزۡقَهُۥۚ بَل لَّجُّواْ فِي عُتُوࣲّ وَنُفُورٍ
67:21.en: Or who is it that could provide for you if He withheld His provision? But they have persisted in insolence and aversion

nOdfk1yNrEg.speaker: adnan
nOdfk1yNrEg.speaker_note: continues his own Ramadan Names of Allah series, moving to the category of provision
nOdfk1yNrEg.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Names of Provision, Al-Razzaq (The Provider)
nOdfk1yNrEg.one_line: Al-Razzaq: everything you have is provision decreed for you, tied in the Quran to need, gratitude, certainty and giving; starvation comes from withheld shares.
nOdfk1yNrEg.summary: He distinguishes Al-Razzaq, the One who provides continuously to all without exception, from the less intensive Ar-Raziq, and defines rizq as anything usable. Rizq becomes a blessing (ni'mah) only when you recognize it as one, so the difference is in your perspective, and everything from your skin colour to your community is rizq. Every creature's provision is upon Allah; Ibrahim's prayer for Mecca was corrected to include disbelievers, and a story has Ibrahim rebuked for evicting a disbelieving guest whom Allah had fed for seventy years. Provisions were measured before humans existed, and no soul dies before using up its share. In the Quran rizq is tied to four ideas: it follows need rather than want, it calls for gratitude that means using it as Allah wants, it is certain enough that Allah swears by it, and it must be given before death brings regret. Rizq includes time, knowledge and attention, not just money. The sardine run and a drop of water travelling the globe to your mouth illustrate decreed provision. People starve because their share sits in others' hands, as with unpaid zakat, and there is enough food for all but not for greed. He asks people to never compromise for rizq, earn only halal, be content while working hard, and become a source of provision for others.

outline.heading: Al-Razzaq versus Ar-Raziq
outline.gist: The intensive form means continuous provision to all without exception, while the simple form carries no such sense.

outline.heading: What rizq means
outline.gist: Rizq is anything usable, even if not beneficial; he asks what separates rizq from ni'mah.

outline.heading: Rizq becomes ni'mah when you see it
outline.gist: The only difference is perspective: acknowledging provision as a blessing makes it ni'mah.

outline.heading: Everything you were given is rizq
outline.gist: Skin, height, parents, birthplace, friends and community are all provision; how much you recognize as blessing depends on you.

outline.heading: Provision is upon Allah
outline.gist: Understand at least each category of names; no creature on earth except that its provision is Allah's responsibility.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's prayer for the barren valley
outline.gist: Ibrahim left his family by the sacred house so they would pray, asking that people come to them and fruits sustain them.

outline.heading: The house existed before Ibrahim
outline.gist: He named the sacred house before building it, because Adam had built it and Ibrahim only rebuilt it.

outline.heading: Provision for disbelievers too
outline.gist: Ibrahim asked fruits for believers only; Allah corrected him that He provides for those who disbelieve as well.

outline.heading: Ibrahim and the disbelieving guest
outline.gist: Ibrahim threw out an old man who denied God; Allah rebuked him for refusing one night to someone He had fed for seventy years.

outline.heading: Provisions measured before creation
outline.gist: Allah assigned the earth's sustenance before humans existed; He creates, provides, causes death and gives life, which no partner can do.

outline.heading: No soul dies before its provision ends
outline.gist: Jibril inspired the Prophet that no soul dies until it has used up all the provision decreed for it.

outline.heading: Rizq written in the womb
outline.gist: The angel who breathes the soul into the fetus writes its provision among four decrees.

outline.heading: First theme: what you need, not what you want
outline.gist: Allah extends and restricts provision for His servant's sake; abundance and scarcity are both for your benefit.

outline.heading: Second theme: gratitude
outline.gist: Hamd is saying alhamdulillah; shukr is using what you were given in the way that pleases Allah and benefits others.

outline.heading: Countless blessings, little gratitude
outline.gist: Heavens, rain, ships, sun, moon and night were subjected for us; seek provision only from Allah and eat of the good and thank Him.

outline.heading: Third theme: certainty
outline.gist: Your provision is in the heavens and Allah swears it is true; a bedouin asked what people did to make the Generous One swear.

outline.heading: Fourth theme: giving before death
outline.gist: Give before you wish on your deathbed to return and give; rizq includes knowledge, time, expertise and listening.

outline.heading: Seeing yourself through a lens of poverty
outline.gist: If your bank account is your most valuable possession you have made yourself poor; the dead wish they had given time, service and emotion.

outline.heading: The sardine run
outline.gist: Sardines swim the same route every year to be eaten by predators that wait for them: provision for those you do not provide for.

outline.heading: A drop of water with your name on it
outline.gist: A drop evaporates over the Pacific, rains on Europe's mountains, is bottled and shipped to Canada, and ends up in your mouth because it was decreed.

outline.heading: Why do people starve?
outline.gist: No one provides if Allah withholds, yet famine and war starvation happen because Allah placed their provision in others' hands.

outline.heading: Zakat is someone else's provision
outline.gist: After a lunar year part of your wealth belongs to others; holding it back withholds their rizq, and you will answer for it.

outline.heading: Enough for bellies, not for greed
outline.gist: There is enough food for many times our numbers; starvation in hard times comes from people holding back each other's provision.

outline.heading: First: never compromise for rizq
outline.gist: Do not fear for your provision or give up who you are for it; bring only halal into your home and your children's bodies.

outline.heading: The provider's job; contentment and hard work
outline.gist: Allah provides, a man's job is to ensure it is halal; be content with what you get while working hard and asking for more.

outline.heading: Halal earnings and accepted dua; be someone's provision
outline.gist: The man who raises his hands while eating and dressing in haram is not answered; give from what you receive and be a source of provision.

outline.heading: Refuge from disbelief and poverty
outline.gist: The Prophet paired them in his dua because it is hard to speak of God to the starving, and poverty comes from human greed.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Al-Razzaq as continuous provider to all, and rizq as everything decreed for you.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Rizq becomes blessing only when you recognize it.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Shukr means using provision as Allah wants, not just saying alhamdulillah.

themes.label: Tawakkul: reliance on Allah
themes.note: Provision is sworn by Allah and certain; do not fear for it.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: Give from all forms of rizq before death brings regret.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: Zakat is others' provision held in your wealth; starvation results from withheld shares and greed.

themes.label: Contentment and acceptance (ridha)
themes.note: Provision follows need, and both abundance and scarcity serve you.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Earn only halal, be content while working hard, and do not compromise yourself for money.

A man travels long, dishevelled, raising his hands saying O Lord, while his food, drink and clothing are haram; how can he be answered

What you need, not what you want
Shukr is using it the way He wants

Provision for creatures humans never feed.

Never compromise your values for provision and bring only halal into your home
Be content with what you receive while working hard and asking for more

8:24.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱسۡتَجِيبُواْ لِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ إِذَا دَعَاكُمۡ لِمَا يُحۡيِيكُمۡۖ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡمَرۡءِ وَقَلۡبِهِۦ وَأَنَّهُۥٓ إِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
8:24.en: O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart and that to Him you will be gathered

0xwVu6Fc8VM.speaker: adnan
0xwVu6Fc8VM.speaker_note: refers to his ten years as imam in the city and to the census he ran of all London masajid; his usual style
0xwVu6Fc8VM.title: Three Ramadanic Reminders
0xwVu6Fc8VM.one_line: Using a citywide taraweeh head-count, he gives three Ramadan reminders: renew your intention, invest in the youth Allah brought, and back dua with action.
0xwVu6Fc8VM.summary: He opens with a census he ran across the city's masajid: about 6,500 people pray taraweeh nightly in Ramadan, against roughly 400 the rest of the year, and most drop off afterwards. Only Allah can turn hearts that quickly, he argues, and this also explains why the Prophet's khutbahs were short: his community lived year-round the way ours lives only in Ramadan. Ramadan is a push Allah gives, but staying afterwards is our responsibility. He then gives three reminders. First, renew your intention every Jumuah of the month; if your relationship with Allah is not enough, do it for yourself, or for the tens of thousands killed in Gaza, because rituals were never meant to be cut off from the condition of the ummah. Second, he cautiously hopes the crowds signal a youth-driven awakening, notes that every revival in Muslim history was led by the young, and warns that masajid must open their minds and hearts, accepting young people with their flaws and doing the hard, unglamorous work of mentoring them, or they will leave. Third, asking Allah for victory while doing nothing toward it is disrespectful, so every such dua needs an action plan. He closes with Abu Hanifah's quiet rescue of his drunk neighbour, who became a scholar.

outline.heading: Opening
Respond to what gives you life (8:24)
outline.gist: Answer Allah and His Messenger when they call you to what gives you life, meaning spiritual life; Allah stands between you and your heart and you will be gathered to Him.

outline.heading: 6,500 in Ramadan, 400 outside it
outline.gist: He had every imam and centre manager estimate taraweeh attendance: about 6,500 nightly, the highest in his ten years, against about 400 outside Ramadan. A caller invites seekers of good to come near.

outline.heading: Only Allah turns hearts this fast
outline.gist: Who else could move a city from 400 to 6,500 in one night? Only the King of Kings, who holds His servants' hearts between two of His fingers.

outline.heading: Why the Prophet's khutbahs were short
outline.gist: His recorded khutbahs are concise, naming deficits and next steps, because his community lived year-round the way ours lives only in Ramadan.

outline.heading: Allah brought you; staying is your job
outline.gist: Attendance drops 70 to 80 percent after the month. Ramadan, with Paradise open and Shaytan chained, is a boost Allah gives; afterwards it is on you to keep coming and find your piece of the puzzle.

outline.heading: A full masjid needs only a short reminder
outline.gist: When people are already volunteering, reading and serving, a brief pointer is enough; after Ramadan the drop-off forces long appeals to come back. He sets out three reminders.

outline.heading: Reminder one: renew your intention
outline.gist: Every Jumuah of the month is a milestone for renewing intention. Fasting while working or studying and standing at night take a toll, so know why you are doing it.

outline.heading: Do it for the people of Gaza
outline.gist: If Allah's love is not enough, do it for yourself, or for the 31,000 killed under the rubble of their homes for sharing your faith and refusing to leave their land.

outline.heading: Rituals were never cut off from the ummah
outline.gist: Once Islam becomes private rituals detached from the state of the nation of Muhammad, we fail. Zoom out of your bubble and let the bigger picture shape your intention.

outline.heading: Interlude
Reminder two: a youth-driven awakening?
outline.gist: Tickling an optimism long dead, he wonders whether the numbers show a modern awakening of young people who refuse to accept the world as it is.

outline.heading: Masjids designed to embrace the young
outline.gist: An awakening needs institutions that take young people in and harness their energy. The five-year-old who annoys you now is the fifteen-year-old you will beg to come back.

outline.heading: Every revival was led by the young
outline.gist: Check the ages of the generals, rulers and scholars we admire: many were strikingly young. The ummah has never had an awakening that was not youth-driven; elders can only support it.

outline.heading: Open minds and hearts, not just doors
outline.gist: Older generations offer wisdom, wealth and advice. The openness that matters is of mind and heart: young people arrive with good and bad habits, and a closed heart sends them away after one visit.

outline.heading: Youth talk is empty without the work
outline.gist: Unless masjids accept the bad with tenderness and patience they will not get the good. Every institution talks about youth, but the work is exhausting and often done alone.

outline.heading: Allah brought them to you: do your job
outline.gist: Mentoring is unglamorous work nobody wants, yet most of the 6,500 are young. Allah delivered them, so embrace, teach and empower them; the future is what we build today.

outline.heading: Interlude
Reminder three: dua for what He asked of you
outline.gist: Dua that pours out pain needs nothing more; it is therapeutic. But asking Allah for victory and prosperity that He commanded us to work for is a different matter.

outline.heading: An action plan: many ways to contribute
outline.gist: Without a plan for how you will contribute, the dua rings hollow. Not everyone serves politically or militarily; education, mentorship, wealth, volunteering, outreach and advocacy all count.

outline.heading: Walking where He told you to go
outline.gist: Asking Allah to do what you are too busy for is improper. A proper dua says: I am walking in the direction You told me, so grant me success.

outline.heading: Abu Hanifah and his drunk neighbour
outline.gist: A young cobbler drank nightly and sang of being neglected. When he was jailed, Abu Hanifah rode to the governor, had him and every prisoner of that night released, and rode him home in silence.

outline.heading: Did I neglect you?
outline.gist: Abu Hanifah asked only that; the young man wept, repented and became a known student whose identity was concealed. This is the mentality needed for a better future.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: Ramadan is a season when Allah calls hearts and fills the masajid; it is a push forward, and keeping the momentum after the month is the believer's responsibility.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Renew your intention each Jumuah of Ramadan; find a reason, and if your relationship with Allah feels empty, make the suffering ummah part of your intention.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: The tens of thousands killed under the rubble in Gaza did nothing wrong but share our faith and refuse to leave their land; they deserve that we do better.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: Islam fails when it is reduced to private rituals cut off from the condition of the ummah; zoom out and see yourself as part of something bigger.

themes.label: Youth, their challenges and their role
themes.note: Every awakening in the ummah's history was youth-driven; the older generations can only support, advise and fund, and must invest in the young people Allah has brought.

themes.label: The masjid: its role and etiquette
themes.note: Masajid must be designed to embrace young people; the openness that matters is of mind and heart, and the annoying child who is unwelcome now will not return at fifteen.

themes.label: Dua and invocation
themes.note: Dua of complaint and sorrow needs nothing more, but dua asking Allah for what He commanded us to do needs an action plan beside it, or it becomes disrespectful.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: Abu Hanifah's quiet care for a sinful neighbour, and the concealment of the student's past, model the tender patience that wins people back.

quran.point: Answering Allah and His Messenger when they call to what gives spiritual life; Allah stands between a person and his heart and all will be gathered to Him.

hadith.gist: When Ramadan begins a caller calls out: seeker of good, come forward; seeker of evil, hold back.
The hearts of the servants are between two fingers of the Most Merciful; He turns them as He wills.
In Ramadan the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of Hell are closed and the devils are chained.

maxims: Find your piece of the puzzle
Never were our rituals disconnected from the bigger picture
Zoom out of the bubble you live in
Open the doors of the mind and heart, not just the masjid
No awakening of the ummah was ever not youth driven
This type of dua requires an action plan beside it

stories.point: His recorded khutbahs are short because his community lived year-round with the commitment we see only in Ramadan.

stories.who: Young leaders and scholars of Muslim history
stories.point: Many celebrated figures achieved their work at ages we would not trust with authority; revival always comes from the young.

stories.who: Abu Hanifah and his drunk shoemaker neighbour
stories.point: He never scolded the man, quietly got him released from prison, and asked only whether he had neglected him; the man repented and became a known scholar whose identity was concealed.

contemporary: Citywide census of London, Ontario masajid at the start of Ramadan 2024: about 6,500 nightly worshippers versus about 400 outside Ramadan
70 to 80 percent drop-off in masjid attendance after Ramadan
About 4,000 to 4,500 attend Jumuah across the city weekly
Gaza: about 31,000 killed by March 2024

Keep coming to the masjid after Ramadan and find your role in serving it
Welcome and mentor young people with their flaws; do the hard work, not just the talk
Pair every dua for the ummah's success with a personal action plan to contribute

5:21.ar: يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ ٱلۡمُقَدَّسَةَ ٱلَّتِي كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ وَلَا تَرۡتَدُّواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَدۡبَارِكُمۡ فَتَنقَلِبُواْ خَٰسِرِينَ
5:21.en: O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has assigned to you and do not turn back [from fighting in Allah 's cause] and [thus] become losers

5:22.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ فِيهَا قَوۡمࣰ ا جَبَّارِينَ وَإِنَّا لَن نَّدۡخُلَهَا حَتَّىٰ يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡهَا فَإِن يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡهَا فَإِنَّا دَٰخِلُونَ
5:22.en: They said, "O Moses, indeed within it is a people of tyrannical strength, and indeed, we will never enter it until they leave it; but if they leave it, then we will enter

5:23.ar: قَالَ رَجُلَانِ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمَا ٱدۡخُلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡبَابَ فَإِذَا دَخَلۡتُمُوهُ فَإِنَّكُمۡ غَٰلِبُونَۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَتَوَكَّلُوٓاْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
5:23.en: Said two men from those who feared [to disobey] upon whom Allah had bestowed favor, "Enter upon them through the gate, for when you have entered it, you will be predominant. And upon Allah rely, if you should be believers

5:24.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَن نَّدۡخُلَهَآ أَبَدࣰ ا مَّا دَامُواْ فِيهَا فَٱذۡهَبۡ أَنتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَٰتِلَآ إِنَّا هَٰهُنَا قَٰعِدُونَ
5:24.en: They said, "O Moses, indeed we will not enter it, ever, as long as they are within it; so go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are remaining right here

5:25.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لَآ أَمۡلِكُ إِلَّا نَفۡسِي وَأَخِيۖ فَٱفۡرُقۡ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
5:25.en: [Moses] said, "My Lord, indeed I do not possess except myself and my brother, so part us from the defiantly disobedient people

5:26.ar: قَالَ فَإِنَّهَا مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡۛ أَرۡبَعِينَ سَنَةࣰۛ يَتِيهُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ فَلَا تَأۡسَ عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
5:26.en: [Allah] said, "Then indeed, it is forbidden to them for forty years [in which] they will wander throughout the land. So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people

5:32.ar: مِنۡ أَجۡلِ ذَٰلِكَ كَتَبۡنَا عَلَىٰ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ أَنَّهُۥ مَن قَتَلَ نَفۡسَۢا بِغَيۡرِ نَفۡسٍ أَوۡ فَسَادࣲ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَمَنۡ أَحۡيَاهَا فَكَأَنَّمَآ أَحۡيَا ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعࣰ اۚ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَتۡهُمۡ رُسُلُنَا بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُم بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَمُسۡرِفُونَ
5:32.en: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption [done] in the land - it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. And whoever saves one - it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And our messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs. Then indeed many of them, [even] after that, throughout the land, were transgressors

5:82.ar: ۞لَتَجِدَنَّ أَشَدَّ ٱلنَّاسِ عَدَٰوَةࣰ لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱلۡيَهُودَ وَٱلَّذِينَ أَشۡرَكُواْۖ وَلَتَجِدَنَّ أَقۡرَبَهُم مَّوَدَّةࣰ لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا نَصَٰرَىٰۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ مِنۡهُمۡ قِسِّيسِينَ وَرُهۡبَانࣰ ا وَأَنَّهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ
5:82.en: You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers [to be] the Jews and those who associate others with Allah; and you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant

5:100.ar: قُل لَّا يَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡخَبِيثُ وَٱلطَّيِّبُ وَلَوۡ أَعۡجَبَكَ كَثۡرَةُ ٱلۡخَبِيثِۚ فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
5:100.en: Say, "Not equal are the evil and the good, although the abundance of evil might impress you." So fear Allah, O you of understanding, that you may be successful

6:8.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَوۡلَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيۡهِ مَلَكࣱۖ وَلَوۡ أَنزَلۡنَا مَلَكࣰ ا لَّقُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ ثُمَّ لَا يُنظَرُونَ
6:8.en: And they say, "Why was there not sent down to him an angel?" But if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided; then they would not be reprieved

6:9.ar: وَلَوۡ جَعَلۡنَٰهُ مَلَكࣰ ا لَّجَعَلۡنَٰهُ رَجُلࣰ ا وَلَلَبَسۡنَا عَلَيۡهِم مَّا يَلۡبِسُونَ
6:9.en: And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him [appear as] a man, and We would have covered them with that in which they cover themselves

5:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَوۡفُواْ بِٱلۡعُقُودِۚ أُحِلَّتۡ لَكُم بَهِيمَةُ ٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ إِلَّا مَا يُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡكُمۡ غَيۡرَ مُحِلِّي ٱلصَّيۡدِ وَأَنتُمۡ حُرُمٌۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحۡكُمُ مَا يُرِيدُ
5:1.en: O you who have believed, fulfill [all] contracts. Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock except for that which is recited to you [in this Qur'an] - hunting not being permitted while you are in the state of ihram. Indeed, Allah ordains what He intends

5:27.ar: ۞وَٱتۡلُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ نَبَأَ ٱبۡنَيۡ ءَادَمَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ إِذۡ قَرَّبَا قُرۡبَانࣰ ا فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنۡ أَحَدِهِمَا وَلَمۡ يُتَقَبَّلۡ مِنَ ٱلۡأٓخَرِ قَالَ لَأَقۡتُلَنَّكَۖ قَالَ إِنَّمَا يَتَقَبَّلُ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
5:27.en: And recite to them the story of Adam's two sons, in truth, when they both offered a sacrifice [to Allah], and it was accepted from one of them but was not accepted from the other. Said [the latter], "I will surely kill you." Said [the former], "Indeed, Allah only accepts from the righteous [who fear Him]

5:28.ar: لَئِنۢ بَسَطتَ إِلَيَّ يَدَكَ لِتَقۡتُلَنِي مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطࣲ يَدِيَ إِلَيۡكَ لِأَقۡتُلَكَۖ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
5:28.en: If you should raise your hand against me to kill me - I shall not raise my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds

5:29.ar: إِنِّيٓ أُرِيدُ أَن تَبُوٓأَ بِإِثۡمِي وَإِثۡمِكَ فَتَكُونَ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلنَّارِۚ وَذَٰلِكَ جَزَٰٓؤُاْ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
5:29.en: Indeed I want you to obtain [thereby] my sin and your sin so you will be among the companions of the Fire. And that is the recompense of wrongdoers

5:30.ar: فَطَوَّعَتۡ لَهُۥ نَفۡسُهُۥ قَتۡلَ أَخِيهِ فَقَتَلَهُۥ فَأَصۡبَحَ مِنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
5:30.en: And his soul permitted to him the murder of his brother, so he killed him and became among the losers

5:31.ar: فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ غُرَابࣰ ا يَبۡحَثُ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لِيُرِيَهُۥ كَيۡفَ يُوَٰرِي سَوۡءَةَ أَخِيهِۚ قَالَ يَٰوَيۡلَتَىٰٓ أَعَجَزۡتُ أَنۡ أَكُونَ مِثۡلَ هَٰذَا ٱلۡغُرَابِ فَأُوَٰرِيَ سَوۡءَةَ أَخِيۖ فَأَصۡبَحَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰدِمِينَ
5:31.en: Then Allah sent a crow searching in the ground to show him how to hide the disgrace of his brother. He said, "O woe to me! Have I failed to be like this crow and hide the body of my brother?" And he became of the regretful

3LCJmaVWJG0.speaker: adnan
3LCJmaVWJG0.speaker_note: Ramadan Quranic Reflections night at MWN; speaks as the imam of the community
3LCJmaVWJG0.title: Ramadan 2024 Night 6: Quranic Reflections on Al-Ma'idah and Al-An'am
3LCJmaVWJG0.one_line: Al-Ma'idah as the contract of Islam: good versus rotten, belief without seeing angels, the sanctity of every life, misused verses, and action with dua.
3LCJmaVWJG0.summary: He presents Al-Ma'idah as the contract placed in the believer's hand: a sequence of commands that protect the five necessities and fit human nature, which Allah knows best. From 5:100 he argues that good and rotten are never equal, however flashy or popular the rotten becomes, and urges young people to judge by merit, not by numbers. From 6:8-9 he explains why angels are not sent visibly: belief means reasoning from signs, and obedience after seeing proves nothing. In 5:32, coming straight after the story of Adam's two sons, he finds the universal sanctity of life: denying it to one person denies it to all, and granting life includes jobs, health care, education and defending the oppressed. He then corrects the use of 5:82 to justify hatred: the verse tells Muslims who will see them as enemies so they can plan, not whom to hate, and an enemy is anyone who denies your right to exist, Muslim or not. He insists the Palestinian claim needs no scripture, and closes with Bani Israel at the gates of Jerusalem, warning that a community which asks Allah, or its imam, to do its work without a plan of its own repeats their mistake.

outline.heading: Opening
Al-Ma'idah puts the pen in your hand
outline.gist: After identity, method, protection and values, this surah gives the detailed terms; it has the most calls to the believers, each a command of its own.

outline.heading: The surah of covenants covers every part of life
outline.gist: Inheritance, struggle, political alliances and duties to self and nation all appear as terms of the contract.

outline.heading: The five necessities the commands protect
outline.gist: Faith, life, intellect, dignity and wealth are each safeguarded by the surah's commands.

outline.heading: Commands in keeping with human nature
outline.gist: Allah knows our urges and weaknesses; the stories of cowardice and envy in the surah show commands designed to tame the worst in us and bring out the best.

outline.heading: Why it is called the Table
outline.gist: The table of Isa's story becomes a symbol of everything Islam lays out, like putting all the cards on the table before you sign.

outline.heading: Legitimate difference versus good and rotten
outline.gist: Many matters allow several valid opinions, but the good and the rotten are never equal, and rot sits on the inside.

outline.heading: Do not be impressed by decorated rot
outline.gist: People of intellect must see past lights, abundance and strength; the rotten stays rotten whoever owns it.

outline.heading: Goodness is not decided by majority
outline.gist: Good and bad are judged objectively on merit once bias and desire are set aside, not by how many support something.

outline.heading: Stand by the good even if alone
outline.gist: Young people should learn to identify the good and hold to it even as the last person on earth who does.

outline.heading: An angel would come looking like a man
outline.gist: Seeing angels or the unseen ends belief; belief means drawing a conclusion from clues, not seeing a colour in front of you.

outline.heading: The point of the test is reasoning toward Allah
outline.gist: Reward depends on reaching Allah through signs and reason; everyone is devout on the Day of Judgment and that is not heroic.

outline.heading: Why prophets warned against demanding miracles
outline.gist: A physical sign that is rejected brings immediate destruction with no time to repent, as with the demanded she-camel.

outline.heading: Sanctity of life after the story of Adam's sons
outline.gist: The verse protecting life comes after Qabil kills his brother out of envy.

outline.heading: The first killer shares in every unjust killing
outline.gist: Whoever starts an evil banks its sin, so Adam's son bears a share of every unjust killing until the Last Day.

outline.heading: Killing one is killing all: an all-or-nothing value
outline.gist: Anyone willing to take one innocent life holds no life sacred; every human and every living thing must be respected.

outline.heading: A universal decree addressed to Bani Israel
outline.gist: The irony that the command came to Bani Israel; no person is inferior or superior in the value of their life.

outline.heading: Ways of granting life to people
outline.gist: Defending the oppressed, health care, feeding the hungry, finding someone a job, clean water and education all count as saving all humanity.

outline.heading: One human family descended from Adam
outline.gist: Placing the verse after the sons of Adam rules out limiting it to one group; then many still transgress after clear signs.

outline.heading: Who will see you as enemies, not whom to hate
outline.gist: The verse says some groups will be hostile toward believers; it is misread as a command to treat them as enemies.

outline.heading: Knowing who dislikes you helps you deal with them
outline.gist: A rational person adjusts with care toward those who dislike him; Muslims hate no one, and using the verse for an agenda is political.

outline.heading: The Jewish faith as the closest relatives
outline.gist: No two groups share more lineage, creed and law than Muslims and Jews, so they are never enemies by belief.

outline.heading: Followers of Isa and quicker alliances
outline.gist: Christians who are not arrogant will feel affinity, which tells Muslims where alliances can be built.

outline.heading: Your enemy is whoever denies your right to exist
outline.gist: Enmity is never by birth, race or belief; many such enemies are Muslim rulers who drove their people out.

outline.heading: Remember why we are on this land
outline.gist: Muslims in North America live on land taken from its first people because they could not live in their own; teach children this while respecting the land.

outline.heading: Plan accordingly and never preach hatred
outline.gist: The verse is information to plan with, and Muslims failed to plan; it must never be used for hatred.

outline.heading: Palestinian rights need no scripture
outline.gist: People who have lived in Palestine for two thousand years cannot be removed because of another people's book.

outline.heading: If ancestral claims ruled the world
outline.gist: Taken seriously, such claims would empty North America and send everyone back to ancient origins.

outline.heading: Musa at the gates of Jerusalem
outline.gist: Allah promised Bani Israel victory if they simply entered, though they were outnumbered and weaker.

outline.heading: Go you and your Lord and fight
outline.gist: Asking Allah to do what He told you to do, with no plan of your own, was rude and disrespectful toward Him.

outline.heading: Forty years lost in the wilderness
outline.gist: That generation wandered until it died out; Musa and Harun died in the wilderness after educating the generation that retook Jerusalem.

outline.heading: Critics who do not play their part
outline.gist: Community members who only critique the masjid and its imam, and duas made with no plan, come close to that same attitude.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: The purposes behind Allah's commands (maqasid)
themes.note: The surah's commands protect the five necessities and are built around the human nature Allah knows.

themes.label: Values, principles and ethics as a system
themes.note: Good and rotten are judged objectively on merit, never by popularity or how impressive the rotten looks.

themes.label: Youth, their challenges and their role
themes.note: Young people must learn to see through what looks strong and popular and stand by the good even alone.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Belief means reasoning from signs to Allah; visible angels or miracles would end the test.

themes.label: The unlawfulness of harm and protecting others
themes.note: Every life is sacred without exception, and saving or improving one life counts as saving all humanity.

themes.label: Human equality and racism
themes.note: All people descend equally from Adam, so no life is worth less than another.

themes.label: Tolerance, pluralism and dealing with difference
themes.note: Muslims hate no one by faith or race; 5:82 is guidance for planning relations with Jews, pagans and Christians, not a call to enmity.

themes.label: Muslim identity and life in the West / Canada
themes.note: Muslims should remember they live on land taken from its first people because they were pushed out of their own.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: The Palestinians' right to their land rests on millennia of living there, not on scriptural argument.

themes.label: Agency, responsibility and rejecting victim mentality
themes.note: Asking Allah or the imam to do the work without one's own plan or contribution repeats Bani Israel's error.

quran.point: The surah opens by commanding believers to fulfil their contracts, which names its theme.
The story of Adam's two sons and the murder out of envy that precedes the decree on life.

hadith.gist: No soul is killed unjustly except that the first son of Adam bears a share of its sin, because he was the first to establish killing.
Whoever starts a bad practice carries its burden and that of those who follow it, as whoever starts a good one earns its reward.

maxims: Rot is always on the inside of things
Goodness has never been based on how many support it
Everyone or no one: an all-in or all-out situation
There is nothing heroic about believing after you see
Plan accordingly
Where's your part?

stories.who: Thamud demanding a she-camel from the rock
stories.point: A miracle that is demanded and then rejected brings destruction with no second chance.
The first murder, done out of envy, frames the sanctity of every human life.

stories.who: Bani Israel refusing to enter Jerusalem
stories.point: Telling Musa to go fight with his Lord shows the rudeness of asking Allah to do what He asked of you.

stories.who: Forty years of wandering; deaths of Musa and Harun
stories.point: The faithless generation died out while the prophets educated a new one that succeeded.
